**Synopsis:**
Treasury Secretary Bessent doubled long-end Treasury buybacks ($4B/operation, 10–30yr maturities) to suppress rising long-dated yields. This creates a visible tension with Fed Chair Warsh's monetary policy stance: Warsh wants markets to set yields freely, is skeptical of balance sheet expansion, and is fighting inflation still well above the 2% target. Market participants currently see the bar for Fed intervention as very high, affirming the Fed retains control of short-term rates. Critics note Treasury buybacks lack a credible strategy to address the structural drivers of elevated yields — AI capex competition, deficit concerns, and a record $40T sovereign debt load.
